items.title: Landweber iteration with discrepancy and budget statuses
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, as required for the Hilbert-space adjoint in the
iteration.

Let $X,Y$ be real or complex Hilbert spaces, let $A:X\to Y$ be a nonzero
compact linear operator, and let $\omega$ satisfy
$0<\omega<2/\|A\|^2$. The input consists of data $y_\delta\in Y$, a noise
bound $\delta\ge0$, a discrepancy factor $\tau>1$, and a finite iteration
budget $N\in\mathbb N$. Define the associated infinite mathematical path by
$x_0=0$ and
$$x_{k+1}=x_k+\omega A^*(y_\delta-Ax_k),\qquad k\ge0.$$
For the finite procedure, evaluate only the prefix through index $N$, in
increasing order, and return at its first stopping condition. Values of the
mathematical path after an earlier return remain defined by the recurrence but
need not be computed by an implementation.

For $k=0,\ldots,N$ in increasing order, compute
$r_k=y_\delta-Ax_k$. If $\|r_k\|\le\tau\delta$, return
$(x_k,k,\texttt{discrepancy})$. If $k=N$, return
$(x_k,k,\texttt{budget-exhausted})$. Otherwise set
$$x_{k+1}=x_k+\omega A^*(y_\delta-Ax_k).$$

The procedure uses exact Hilbert-space operations. It reports a finite-budget
failure to cross as inconclusive; that status is not a convergence conclusion.
items.strategy: Give the finite inputs and every return branch; define the mathematical recurrence path through the budget and distinguish the lazy early return from its continuation.

items.title: Exact-arithmetic LSQR with Golub–Kahan bidiagonalization and explicit statuses
items.statement:
Let $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$, $b\in\mathbb R^m$, $x_0\in\mathbb R^n$,
$\delta\ge0$, $\tau>1$, and a budget $N\in\mathbb N$ be given. All
operations are exact. Put $r_0=b-Ax_0$. If $\|r_0\|_2=0$, return
$(x_0,0,\text{zero-residual})$. If $\|r_0\|_2\le\tau\delta$, return
$(x_0,0,\text{discrepancy})$. If $N=0$, return
$(x_0,0,\text{budget-exhausted})$. Otherwise initialize
$\beta_1=\|r_0\|_2$, $u_1=r_0/\beta_1$, and
$\alpha_1=\|A^Tu_1\|_2$. If $\alpha_1=0$, return
$(x_0,0,\text{stationary-nonzero-residual})$. Otherwise set
$v_1=A^Tu_1/\alpha_1$.

Initialize the current best iterate and index to $(x_{\rm best},j_{\rm best})
=(x_0,0)$. If a Givens rotation is undefined, return
$(x_{\rm best},j_{\rm best},\text{small-QR-breakdown})$.

For $j=1,\ldots,N$, perform these steps.

1. Compute $p_j=Av_j-\alpha_j u_j$ and $\beta_{j+1}=\|p_j\|_2$. If
   $\beta_{j+1}>0$, set $u_{j+1}=p_j/\beta_{j+1}$.
2. If $\beta_{j+1}>0$, compute
   $q_j=A^Tu_{j+1}-\beta_{j+1}v_j$ and $\alpha_{j+1}=\|q_j\|_2$. If
   $\alpha_{j+1}>0$, set $v_{j+1}=q_j/\alpha_{j+1}$. A zero
   $\beta_{j+1}$ or $\alpha_{j+1}$ marks bidiagonalization breakdown.
3. Form the $(j+1)\times j$ lower-bidiagonal matrix $B_j$ with diagonal
   $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_j$ and subdiagonal
   $\beta_2,\ldots,\beta_{j+1}$, using $\beta_{j+1}=0$ if step 1 broke down.
   Let $e_1=(1,0,\ldots,0)^T\in\mathbb R^{j+1}$ and $c=\beta_1e_1$.
   For $i=1,\ldots,j$, let $a,b$ be the current entries at positions
   $(i,i),(i+1,i)$ of the rotated matrix and put $\rho=(a^2+b^2)^{1/2}$.
   If $\rho=0$, return the current best output with status
   `small-QR-breakdown`. Otherwise put $c_i=a/\rho$, $s_i=b/\rho$ and
   apply $\begin{pmatrix}c_i&s_i\\-s_i&c_i\end{pmatrix}$ to rows
   $i,i+1$ of the full matrix and right-hand side. After these $j$ rotations,
   let $R_j$ be the first $j$ rows of the rotated matrix and $d_j$ the first
   $j$ entries of the rotated right-hand side. Solve $R_jz_j=d_j$ by back
   substitution. Update $(x_{\rm best},j_{\rm best})=(x_0+V_jz_j,j)$.
4. Put $V_j=[v_1,\ldots,v_j]$ and $x_j=x_0+V_jz_j$. Compute the physical
   residual $\|Ax_j-b\|_2$. If it is at most $\tau\delta$, return
   $(x_j,j,\text{discrepancy})$. If bidiagonalization broke down, return
   $(x_j,j,\text{bidiagonalization-breakdown})$. If $j=N$, return
   $(x_j,j,\text{budget-exhausted})$; otherwise continue.

The procedure makes no claim that a finite-budget status is a successful
regularized approximation. Its exact-arithmetic residual-minimization property
is a separate theorem.
items.strategy: State the matrix/vector domains, all zero branches, the bidiagonal recurrence, the exact row rotations, triangular solve, physical residual test, and outputs. Claim no finite-precision stability.

items.title: A Lipschitz Fréchet derivative gives a quadratic linearization remainder
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$ and let
$X,Y$ be Banach spaces over the same field $\mathbb F$. Let $U\subseteq X$ be
open and let $F:U\to Y$ be continuously Fréchet differentiable over
$\mathbb F$. Thus $F'(u)$ is bounded $\mathbb F$-linear for each $u\in U$ and
$$\lim_{\substack{h\to0,\ h\ne0\\u+h\in U}}
\frac{\|F(u+h)-F(u)-F'(u)h\|}{\|h\|}=0.$$
In particular, in the complex case $F'(u)$ is complex-linear and the limit
ranges over complex increments. Let $K\subseteq U$ be convex and let
$x,z\in K$. If
$\|F'(u)-F'(v)\|\le L\|u-v\|$ for all $u,v\in K$, where $L\ge0$, then
$$\|F(x)-F(z)-F'(z)(x-z)\|\le\frac L2\|x-z\|^2.$$
items.strategy: Parametrize the segment from z to x, apply the Banach-valued fundamental theorem of calculus, subtract the constant derivative integral, and integrate the Lipschitz bound.

items.title: Unanchored Levenberg–Marquardt step with explicit early stopping
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, as required for the Hilbert-space adjoints in the
normal equation.

Let $X,Y$ be Hilbert spaces over the same field $\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$,
let $U\subseteq X$ be open, and let $F:U\to Y$ be continuously Fréchet
differentiable over $\mathbb F$. In the complex case, each $F'(x)$ is a bounded
complex-linear operator and the Fréchet remainder is measured over complex
increments, so
$$\lim_{\substack{h\to0,\ h\ne0\\x+h\in U}}
\frac{\|F(x+h)-F(x)-F'(x)h\|}{\|h\|}=0.$$
Inputs are
$x_0\in U$, noisy data $y_\delta\in Y$, a bound $\delta\ge0$, a discrepancy
factor $\tau>1$, a finite budget $N\in\mathbb N$, and parameters
$\alpha_0>0$ and $q\in(0,1)$. At iteration $k$, if $x_k\notin U$ return
$(x_k,k,\text{domain-failure})$. Otherwise put $A_k=F'(x_k)$ and
$\alpha_k=\alpha_0q^k$. Before computing an update, if
$\|F(x_k)-y_\delta\|\le\tau\delta$, return
$(x_k,k,\text{discrepancy})$. If $k=N$, return
$(x_k,k,\text{budget-exhausted})$.

For $k<N$, solve the unique Hilbert-space Tikhonov normal equation
$$\bigl(A_k^*A_k+\alpha_k I_X\bigr)s_k=A_k^*(y_\delta-F(x_k))$$
and set $x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k$. The shifted normal operator is invertible by
[[lem-hilbert-tikhonov-normal-operator-invertible]]. If the returned iterate
leaves $U$, the next call returns domain-failure. The procedure asserts no
convergence theorem; its prescribed step is the unanchored Levenberg–Marquardt
form used in the assigned contract.
items.strategy: State the open-domain and Hilbert-space inputs, check discrepancy before the solve, use the positive-shift normal inverse, update by x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k, and make no convergence assertion.

items.title: A nonbreakdown LSQR iterate minimizes residual on its Krylov space
items.statement:
Let $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$, $b\in\mathbb R^m$, $x_0\in\mathbb R^n$, and
$r_0=b-Ax_0$. Consider a $k$-step run of
[[alg-golub-kahan-lsqr-with-givens-and-status]] with nonzero initial residual
and no bidiagonalization or small-QR breakdown through step $k$. Then its
iterate $x_k$ minimizes $\|Ax-b\|_2$ over
$$x_0+\mathcal K_k(A^TA,A^Tr_0),$$
where $\mathcal K_k(M,v)=\operatorname{span}\{v,Mv,\ldots,M^{k-1}v\}$ is the
Krylov subspace of [[def-krylov-subspace-of-a-matrix-and-start-vector]].
The assertion is exact-arithmetic residual minimization; it is not a
convergence or noise-stability theorem.
items.strategy: Prove the two orthogonality recurrences by induction, assemble the bidiagonal projection and norm identity, transfer the projected least-squares minimizer, and identify the basis span with the Krylov space.

items.title: Landweber iterates and residuals are spectral-filter iterates
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $A:X\to Y$ and $\omega$ satisfy the
hypotheses of [[alg-landweber-iteration-with-discrepancy-stopping]] and put
$T=A^*A$. For each integer $k\ge0$, define
$g_0(t)=0$ and
$g_k(t)=\omega\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}(1-\omega t)^j$ for $k\ge1$, with
$r_k(t)=(1-\omega t)^k$. For the associated infinite mathematical path,
$$x_k=g_k(T)A^*y_\delta,\qquad y_\delta-Ax_k=r_k(AA^*)y_\delta.$$
If $y_\delta=Ax^\dagger$, then
$$x^\dagger-x_k=r_k(T)x^\dagger.$$
Here $g_k(T)$ and $r_k(T)$ are the compact spectral multipliers defined in
[[def-compact-spectral-filter-and-qualification]]; $r_k(AA^*)$ is the
multiplier with scalar function $t\mapsto(1-\omega t)^k$ on the compact
self-adjoint operator $AA^*$, as supplied by
[[lem-compact-spectral-multiplier-is-well-defined]].
items.strategy: Induct on the vector recurrence and residual recurrence, then use the finite geometric identity to identify g_k and r_k.

items.title: One-step error recurrence for the assigned nonlinear regularized Gauss–Newton step
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $X,Y$ be real or complex Hilbert spaces over the
same scalar field and let $U\subseteq X$ be open. Let $F:U\to Y$ be
continuously Fréchet differentiable over that field, with bounded
complex-linear derivatives in the complex case. Let $x^\dagger\in U$ satisfy
$F(x^\dagger)=y$, and suppose $x_k,x^\dagger$ lie in a convex subset of $U$
on which $F'$ is $L$-Lipschitz. Let $y_\delta$ satisfy
$\|y_\delta-y\|\le\delta$, put $e_k=x_k-x^\dagger$ and $A_k=F'(x_k)$,
and use the step of
[[alg-iteratively-regularized-gauss-newton-step]] with $\alpha_k>0$.
Define
$$R_k:=y-F(x_k)+A_ke_k.$$
Then
$$e_{k+1}=\alpha_k(A_k^*A_k+\alpha_kI)^{-1}e_k +(A_k^*A_k+\alpha_kI)^{-1}A_k^*(y_\delta-y+R_k),$$
and
$$\|e_{k+1}\|\le\|e_k\|+ \frac{\delta+(L/2)\|e_k\|^2}{2\sqrt{\alpha_k}}.$$
If in addition the tangential-cone condition
$$\|F(x)-F(z)-F'(z)(x-z)\|\le\eta\|F(x)-F(z)\|$$
holds for all $x,z$ in that subset, then also
$\|R_k\|\le\eta(\|F(x_k)-y_\delta\|+\delta)$, which may replace
$(L/2)\|e_k\|^2$ in the recurrence bound. This lemma alone does not assert
contraction or discrepancy-stopped convergence.
items.strategy: Multiply the error update by the shifted normal operator, isolate the noise and linearization remainder, then use the supplier norm bounds and triangle inequality.

items.title: Landweber converges for exact data and balances source bias with noise
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $A:X\to Y$ be a nonzero compact operator between
real or complex Hilbert spaces, set $T=A^*A$, choose
$0<\omega<2/\|A\|^2$, and let $y=Ax^\dagger$ with
$x^\dagger\in(\ker A)^\perp$. Let $x_k$ be the exact-data Landweber iterates
in the infinite recurrence-defined path of
[[alg-landweber-iteration-with-discrepancy-stopping]] for datum $y$; this path
depends on $A,\omega,y$ and not on a finite cap or stopping test. Put
$r_k(t)=(1-\omega t)^k$. Then $\|x_k-x^\dagger\|$ is nonincreasing and
$x_k\to x^\dagger$ in norm. For every $s>0$, if $x^\dagger=T^s w$ with
$w\in X$, then for $k\ge1$,
$$\|x_k-x^\dagger\|\le C_{s,A,\omega}\|w\|k^{-s}.$$
The scalar filter also satisfies
$$\sup_{t\in\Sigma}t^s|r_k(t)|\le C_{s,A,\omega}k^{-s},$$
where $\Sigma$ is the set of nonzero eigenvalues of $T$.
For noisy data $y_\delta$ with $\|y_\delta-y\|\le\delta$, let
$x_k^\delta$ be the infinite recurrence-defined path for datum $y_\delta$.
It satisfies
$$\|x_k^\delta-x_k\|\le\sqrt{2\omega k}\,\delta.$$
Consequently, under the source condition $x^\dagger=T^\nu w$,
$0<\nu\le1$, the total error obeys
$$\|x_k^\delta-x^\dagger\|\le C_{\nu,A,\omega}\|w\|k^{-\nu} +\sqrt{2\omega k}\,\delta.$$
items.strategy: Use compact spectral components for monotonicity and convergence, bound the scalar filter multiplier, and estimate the noise operator through Q_k Q_k*.

items.title: Landweber discrepancy stopping converges under a source condition
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the hypotheses of
[[thm-landweber-source-and-noise-error-bounds]]. Let
$x^\dagger=T^\nu w$ with $0<\nu\le1$ and $R=\|w\|\ge0$. Fix $\tau>1$ and
$\delta>0$ with $\|y_\delta-Ax^\dagger\|\le\delta$. Let $k_\delta$ be the
first index on the associated infinite mathematical path satisfying
$\|Ax_{k_\delta}^\delta-y_\delta\|\le\tau\delta$, where $x_k^\delta$ is
the corresponding noisy-data path.
If a finite budget is used, assume it is at least the upper bound $K_\delta$
constructed in the proof when $R>0$. If $R=0$, the initial iterate is the
first crossing and any finite budget suffices. For all sufficiently small
$\delta$,
$$\|x_{k_\delta}^\delta-x^\dagger\| \le C_{\nu,A,\omega,\tau}R^{1/(2\nu+1)}\delta^{2\nu/(2\nu+1)}.$$
The conclusion is conditional on an actual discrepancy crossing; a budget
exhaustion status is inconclusive.
items.strategy: Construct an upper crossing index from the residual source bound, control noise in data space, prove the spectral interpolation inequality on finite eigenvalue sets, and bound the propagated solution noise.

items.title: Real and complex Hilbert source powers and fixed-reference Tikhonov filter bounds
Anchored iteratively regularized Gauss-Newton with finite discrepancy stopping
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $X,Y$ be Hilbert spaces over the same field
$\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, let $U\subseteq X$ be open, and let
$F:U\to Y$ be continuously Fréchet differentiable over $\mathbb F$: for each
$x\in U$, $F'(x)$ is bounded $\mathbb F$-linear, the map $x\mapsto F'(x)$ is
operator-norm continuous, and
$$\lim_{\substack{h\to0,\ h\ne0\\x+h\in U}} \frac{\|F(x+h)-F(x)-F'(x)h\|}{\|h\|}=0,$$
where $h$ ranges over increments in $\mathbb F$. In the complex case the
derivative is complex-linear and the limit uses complex increments.
Inputs are anchor and
initial point $x_0\in U$, datum $y_\delta$, noise bound $\delta\ge0$,
discrepancy factor $\tau>1$, finite update cap $N\in\mathbb N_0$,
$\alpha_0>0$ and $q\in(0,1)$. For $k=0,\ldots,N$, first check $x_k\in U$;
otherwise return $(x_k,k,\texttt{domain-failure})$. The output of every return
is a tuple $(x_k,k,\text{status})$. Use an exact-call interface with these
outcomes: an evaluation call returns either $\texttt{ok}(v_k)$ with the exact
value $v_k=F(x_k)$ or $\texttt{failure}$; a normal-solve call returns either
$\texttt{ok}(s_k)$ with the exact solution of the displayed equation or
$\texttt{unverified}$. The interface never returns an incorrect value. If the
evaluation call returns $\texttt{failure}$, return
$(x_k,k,\texttt{evaluation-failure})$. If the evaluation returns
$\texttt{ok}(v_k)$ and $\|v_k-y_\delta\|\le\tau\delta$, return
$(x_k,k,\texttt{discrepancy})$. If $k=N$, return
$(x_k,k,\texttt{budget-exhausted})$. Otherwise set
$A_k=F'(x_k)$, $\alpha_k=\alpha_0q^k$, and call the normal solver on
$$(A_k^*A_k+\alpha_k I)s_k=A_k^*(y_\delta-v_k)+\alpha_k(x_0-x_k),$$
whose exact solution exists uniquely by [[lem-hilbert-tikhonov-normal-operator-invertible]]. If the solve call returns
$\texttt{unverified}$, return $(x_k,k,\texttt{solve-unverified})$; otherwise
set $x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k$. The mathematical evaluation and solve succeed because
$F$ is defined on $U$ and the shifted normal equation has a unique solution;
the failure outcomes record only a finite implementation's inability to
return the exact value or certify the exact solve. No success or convergence
claim is attached to these failure statuses.

The mathematical extended recurrence means the same exact updates with the discrepancy and finite-cap tests suppressed, for as long as the states lie in $U$. It is used only for comparison in proofs. A finite actual run follows its prefix and stops at its first test crossing. This anchored update is distinct from the retained unanchored Levenberg-Marquardt step; its extra term is $\alpha_k(x_0-x_k)$.

title: Iterative regularization and early stopping — Examples

items.title: A fully converged LSQR solve can amplify a small singular-direction error
items.statement:
There is a constant independent of the matrix such that continuing the LSQR
projected solves to zero residual always gives an estimate within that
constant times the data-noise level of the exact solution.
items.strategy: Compute the one-dimensional weak-singular-direction Golub–Kahan and projected solve exactly, then compare its solution error with the data-noise norm; distinguish the assigned early return.

items.title: One regularized Gauss–Newton step for exponential reaction kinetics
items.statement:
For a first-order reaction with conversion fraction $F(c)=1-e^{-c}$ at unit
time, use $X=Y=U=\mathbb R$, true rate $c^\dagger=\log 2$, exact datum
$y=\tfrac12$, initial rate $c_0=0$, $\alpha_0=\tfrac14$, $q=\tfrac12$,
discrepancy factor $\tau=2$, and budget $N=1$. For
$0<\delta\le\tfrac1{10}$ and $|\varepsilon|\le\delta$, the datum
$y^\delta=\tfrac12+\varepsilon$ does not meet the initial discrepancy stopping condition. The
single update gives $c_1=\tfrac25+\tfrac45\varepsilon$; the procedure returns
this state with status `discrepancy` if its post-update residual is at most
$2\delta$, and otherwise with status `budget-exhausted`.
items.strategy: Differentiate the scalar model with the chain rule, verify exp(log 2)=2, check the initial residual exceeds tau delta, substitute the scalar normal equation, and bound the returned rate below.

items.title: Landweber semiconvergence for diagonal noisy data
items.statement:
Let $I=\{j\in\mathbb N:j\ge1\}$ and $X=Y=\ell^2(I,\mathbb R)$, let $Ae_j=2^{-j}e_j$ for the standard unit
vectors $e_j$, and take $\omega=1$, exact solution $x^\dagger=0$, and exact
data $y=0$. For $\delta>0$ let
$y^\delta_j=\delta\,2^{-j/2}$, so $\|y^\delta-y\|=\delta$. The un-stopped
Landweber residual tends to zero, but the reconstruction norms are unbounded
along the subsequence $k_j=4^j$.
items.strategy: Approximate the diagonal operator by finite-rank truncations, compute residual and reconstruction coordinates, and use a geometric bound on (1-4^-j)^(4^j).

items.title: Landweber reconstructs a three-pixel blurred signal
items.statement:
Consider the symmetric three-pixel averaging blur
$$A=\frac14\begin{pmatrix}2&1&1\\1&2&1\\1&1&2\end{pmatrix}.$$
For the zero-sum signal $x^\dagger=(1,0,-1)^T$, exact data are
$y=Ax^\dagger=\tfrac14x^\dagger$. With $x_0=0$ and $\omega=1$, the
Landweber iterates are $x_k=(1-(15/16)^k)x^\dagger$: the first reconstruction
is only $x_1=\tfrac1{16}x^\dagger$, while the exact signal is recovered in the
limit.
items.strategy: Diagonalize the displayed rank-one perturbation of the identity, verify the step interval, and apply the exact-data Landweber error filter.
